about.title: Alameda Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Alameda is a compact city of roughly 78,630 people, and a large share of its daily driving funnels through a handful of streets. Public collision records for 2025 show 129 injury crashes inside city limits, with 166 people hurt and one life lost. Lincoln Avenue, Buena Vista Avenue, Park Street, and Central Avenue show up most frequently in those records, and reported crashes cluster on Tuesdays between midnight and 2 a.m. These are neutral counts, but each one stands for a person whose week, and sometimes whose year, changed without warning. If that person is you, what happens next matters. California allows two years to file most injury claims, yet evidence such as dashcam footage, skid marks, and witness recollections fades much sooner. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We listen to what happened, then match you with an independent attorney serving Alameda County who takes car accident cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless they recover for you. Whether to proceed stays entirely your call.

whyChoose.title: Why Alameda Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than People Expect
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a claim involving a city, county, or transit vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Connecting early keeps every option on the table.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even a driver found partly responsible can still recover, reduced by their share. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Protection Before You Talk to the Other Insurer
items.desc: The other driver's adjuster may ask for a recorded statement quickly; you are not required to give one. The attorneys in our network work on contingency and can handle those conversations while you focus on recovering.

items.question: What if my Alameda crash involved a city vehicle or a bus?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California often follow a different track, with a written claim generally due within six months rather than the usual two years. Missing that window can close the door on recovery. Because of that, it is worth speaking with an attorney soon after a collision with any publicly owned vehicle in Alameda.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling. Should I give a statement?
items.answer: You are under no obligation to provide a recorded statement to another driver's insurer, and doing so before you understand your injuries can work against you. Simple phrases like "I'm fine" are often used later to minimize a claim. Politely decline, save any voicemails or letters, and let an attorney handle contact once you have one.

items.question: I think I was partly at fault. Is it still worth pursuing a claim?
items.answer: Often, yes. California's pure comparative fault rule means your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated, even if that share is significant. Fault is frequently disputed after crashes on busy streets like Central Avenue, so photos, witness names, and the police report can shape how that percentage is assigned.
